segments.text:
The module comment.
- This file writes sections 4, 5 and 6 of `FACTS.md`. `facts_text.py` uses it.
- The comment says that the text templates hold words only, and that every number is formatted from the collected data.
- A few counts are typed in the templates. Examples are "2 corrected records" in line 510 and "and 1" in line 430. A `need` call tests each of these two counts (lines 293 and 363).
segments.heading: Module comment and imports

segments.text:
Imports. `os` and `re` come from the Python standard library. The module `facts_data.py` is also imported as a whole under the name `fd`.
- From `facts_data.py`: the results folder `R`, the record filter `sel`, the range function `rng`, and `overlap`, `gap` and `width_pct` [Ref2].
- From `facts_text.py`: the check `need`, the number formats `g`, `sp`, `pc`, `pcr` and `_q`, the time formats `hm`, `hmd` and `dur`, the n formats `nn` and `nns`, and `table`, `compare` and `med` [Ref1].
- Also from `facts_text.py`: the row lists `BW12` (L-1 to L-4), `BW11` (R0, R0b) and `BWX` (B7a, B7b, C3a, C3b), the folder `W15`, and the fixed texts.
- `gap` and `sess` are imported and not called in this file.

Two labels for the rows F72d12 and control I in the range tests. `OWN` is the label that the tables of `FACTS.md` print. `OLD_OWN` is the key of the same rows in `facts.json`. The key stays as it was in earlier builds.

Collects the values of the field `min_ms` of the given records, each value once, in rising order. Each value is divided by 1000 and printed in seconds. Several values are joined with `and`. Example: records with `min_ms` 4000 and 6000 give `4 s and 6 s`.
segments.heading: Function `secs`: interval lengths as text

segments.text:
`section4` starts here and ends at line 1615. `facts_text.py` calls it once [Ref1].
- `recs`: the list of all interval records. This file reads no csv row. The rate of a record is its field `GBps`.
- For a part A record `GBps` is the csv column `aggregate_GBps`. The header line of each process in the csv file gives its formula: sum(bytes) / max(per-thread elapsed_s). For a record of a bwx runner it is the sum over the T rows of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9 [Ref2] [Ref3].
- `w`: appends one line of text to the output list `L`.
- `try6`: the reading of 12 modules at 7200 MT/s, with the boot id of the rerun.
- `rules`: the path of the rules file `baselines-and-rules.txt`. `evd`: the steps of `go.sh` and `go2.sh`, by tag.
- `pool`: the function `N['pool']`. It returns the records of several rows for one kernel and position.
segments.heading: Function `section4`: sections 4 to 6 of the facts sheet

segments.text:
Reads the comparisons and the record lists from the context `c`. `facts_text.py` prepared them [Ref1]. In the names, `o` stands for the old read kernel and `a` for asmread.
- Line 31, comparisons against the pool L-1 to L-4: `cLo`, `cLa` (part L), `cIo`, `cIa` (control I), `cFo`, `cFa` (F72d12) and `cCo` (oldread of part C). `cAo` compares `bw_old read` of part A with rows A-1 to A-3.
- Line 32, 7200 MT/s lists: oldread and asmread of part L (`L72o`, `L72a`), of control I (`I72o`, `I72a`) and of F72d12 (`F72o`, `F72a`).
- Line 33, 8000 MT/s lists: `P12o` is oldread at position 0 of rows L-1 to L-4. `P12a` is asmread at position 1 of the same rows. `PALLo` and `PALLa` add rows R0 and R0b. `A80o` is `bw_old read` of rows A-1 to A-3.
- Also line 33, 7200 MT/s lists: `A72o` is `bw_old read` of part A. `C72o` is oldread of part C at every position. That is position 0 in the cfwd processes and position 2 in the crev processes.
- Line 34: `pa3` and `newread` hold the cells of rule V3 (part A, load-only kernels).

- `C`: all records of part C (`dataset` = `rerun-C`).
- `first`: the text that the field `kernel_before` holds for the first interval of a process.
- `CG`: the load-only intervals of part C in five groups (rule V2).
- `f72la`, `fenv`, `f72dir`: for the F72d12 process (tag `a6456`), the entry with its launch line and its rc line, the parsed content of its `env.txt`, and its run folder.
- `S_`: the folder of the rules file. It is folder S.
- `one_v`: a one-line function. For a list with one record it prints the rate with 2 decimal places. For a longer list it prints the lowest to the highest rate.

`src` returns the reference labels of the csv files that hold the given records. It builds each path from the results folder `R`, the field `folder` without its first two characters `R/`, and the field `file`. Each file is named once, in the order of the records. `ref` turns a path into its label `[RefN]`.
segments.heading: Local helpers of `section4`

segments.text:
`ranges` builds a range table with one row per record list `rs`.
- `rng(rs)` gives the lowest value, the highest value and the median of `GBps`, the number of intervals and the number of processes [Ref2]. No mean over intervals is taken.
- The median of an even number of values is the mean of the two middle values.
- Line 53: the build stops unless all records of the list have the same memory speed and the same module count. `build_facts.py` sets both fields (see the explanation of lines 150 to 152).
- The row prints n as intervals / processes, the range as lowest to highest, and the median. `sp` and `g` round to 2 decimal places. A value exactly between two steps is rounded away from zero (half up).
- The last cell names the csv files (`src`).

`source` builds the Source cell of the row table in section 4.1. The cell says where the rates, the load and the sha256 of the binary come from.
- A row written by `rx.sh` or `r0.sh` (a key of `D['rx']`): the csv files for the rates, `launches.txt` for the load, and `env.txt` for the sha256. When `env.txt` holds no binary line, the script `r0.sh` is named for the sha256.
- A row of runner bwx (a key of `D['step']`): the csv file for the rates and the load, and `env.txt` of the folder for the sha256.
- Row A-1: the csv file, and the file `probe.txt` of the 2026-11-13 run for the sha256.
- Rows A-2 and A-3: the csv file, and `env.txt` of the run folder for the sha256.
- The records of rows A-2 and A-3 take their sha256 from the `probe.txt` of row A-1, not from this `env.txt`. `build_facts.py` runs integrity checks (tests of the raw files and the scripts). Its check `sha-bw` tests that this `env.txt` holds the same two values [Ref3]. Line 1461 stops the build unless every integrity check passed.

`cmps` runs the range tests of one part and kernel.
- `items` is a list of 7200 MT/s rows. Each row has a label, its records and a list of scopes.
- A scope is one 8000 MT/s record list with a label and the flag `decides`.
- A label may be a pair: the key for `facts.json` and the text for the table.
segments.heading: Helper `cmps`: the range tests of rule V1 point 2

segments.text:
For each 7200 MT/s row and each scope:
- `compare(r72, r80)` forms the min-to-max range `a` of the 7200 MT/s records and the range `b` of the 8000 MT/s records [Ref1].
- `overlap` is true when `a.lo <= b.hi` and `b.lo <= a.hi`. Two ranges that only share one end value count as an overlap.
- `dist` is the distance of the nearest ends in GB/s. It is positive when the 7200 MT/s range lies above, negative when it lies below, and 0 for an overlap.
- `width` is (b.hi - b.lo) / b.lo x 100: the width of the 8000 MT/s range in percent of its lower end.
- `q2row` stores the test in `V['q2_rows']` for `facts.json`: both ranges, both n, the overlap flag and the distance rounded to 3 decimal places. The stored wording is `None` (no value) unless `decides` is true.
- The note of the stored test is the entry of `notes` for the label. Without such an entry it is `note` when `decides` is true, and empty otherwise.

One table row per test: the 7200 MT/s row and its range, the 8000 MT/s scope and its range, `yes` or `no` for the overlap, the distance, the width and the wording.
- The distance cell is `0` for an overlap. Otherwise it is the signed value with 2 decimal places. It uses the Python format `%+.2f`, not the half-up rounding of `g`.
- The width is printed with 1 decimal place (`pc`).
- The wording is "no difference seen" for an overlap and "differs between the 8000 MT/s boot and the 7200 MT/s boot" otherwise. It is printed only when `decides` is true. Otherwise the cell is `-`.

`DESC` holds one description per earlier row. The row table of section 4.1 and the range tables print it in the column "What it is".
- All entries are template text (words written as they stand in the code), except the entry of F72d12.
- That entry inserts two values: the load at launch of the F72d12 process, and the time from the first Linux kernel log line of the boot to that launch.
- The load comes from `launches.txt`. The time of the first log line comes from `gaps.txt` [Ref2].
segments.heading: Descriptions of the earlier rows, check of the argument lines

segments.text:
Reads the argument lines of `like.spec`, `cfwd.spec` and `crev.spec` from folder S.
- A spec file holds a tag, the character `|` and the arguments. The code keeps the arguments.
- `noseq` removes the value after `--seq` from an argument line.
- Line 124: the build stops unless the three lines are equal after `noseq` and all differ before it.
- Line 125: the build also stops unless the launch line of row L-1 (tag `a6456`) holds exactly the arguments of `like.spec`.
- `L1C`: the description of row L-1 for the tables of part C.

Writes the headings of sections 4 and 4.1 and a summary of the rules: rule V1 points 2, 3 and 4, rule V3, rule V2, and rules V4 and F2. These lines compute no number.
- Line 134 says as template text that the rules were fixed before the run. `facts_text.py` tests it before it calls `section4`. The rules file states the time of its writing. That time must lie before the time of the first state line of the `go.sh` log, and it must equal the file time of the rules file [Ref1].
- The two wordings of rule V1 point 2 are inserted from `DIFFERS` and `SAME`.
- The last bullet says that the rules contradict each other on part C, and that the sheet follows V1, V2 and V4.
segments.heading: Section 4.1: the rules and the rows

segments.text:
Check of the boots.
- `b80`: the boot labels of the records of rows L-1 to L-4, R0, R0b, B7a, B7b, C3a, C3b, A-1, A-2, A-3, B5a and B5b, each label once. A boot label is a text such as `boot -5 of the DIMM report (Linux start 2026-11-09 21:20 UTC)`. Rows B5a-rev and B5b-rev are not in the list of line 150. Their records come from the same two folders as B5a and B5b [Ref3].
- `b72`: the boot ids of all records with a memory speed of 7200 MT/s, each id once.
- Line 152: the build stops unless `b80` holds one label and `b72` holds only the boot id of `try6.txt`.
- `build_facts.py` sets the fields `speed_MTps`, `modules` and `boot` of a record. It does not read them from the files in the run folder [Ref3]. For a row of an earlier run, except F72d12, the three values come from the DIMM report, for the time in the name of the run folder. Every record of the rerun, of control I and of F72d12 gets the memory speed, the number of DIMM sockets and the boot id of `try6.txt`.
- So the `b72` part of line 152 is true whatever the run files contain. It does not prove the boot of a run. The bullet in lines 153 to 156 names the two proofs.
- Other code tests the boot of the 7200 MT/s rows. The integrity check `boot` of `build_facts.py` compares the boot id in every state line of the `go.sh` log and of the `go2.sh` log, and in the three `probe.txt` files of part A, with `try6.txt` [Ref3]. Line 1461 stops the build unless every integrity check passed. Lines 219 to 222 test row F72d12.

- This bullet of the sheet names the one 8000 MT/s boot and the first 8 characters of the 7200 MT/s boot id. It says that the proof for the rerun is in section 1.2, and that the proof for row F72d12 stands under the table.
- Rows X2d12, X1d10, X1d10b and BASEd10 are 8000 MT/s rows that are not in the list of line 150. The bullet says as template text that they come from other boots. No `need` call of this file tests it. In the present sheet the row table gives them boots -2, -4, -3 and -1 of the DIMM report [Ref4].

- `gs` is the list of the state lines of the `go.sh` log.
- The bullet gives the time from the first state line to the last state line as the time within which the three sessions ran. `dur` prints it in hours, minutes and seconds.
- In the present log the last state line is the line `== end`. It stands after the state line of T72C4, the part C process that ran after the three sessions. So the printed time includes that process. Its present value is 10 min 9 s [Ref4].
- Then the title line of the row table is written.

Starts the table of the 22 earlier rows. For each row name `ds`:
- `rs`: all records with this `dataset`.
- `procs`: the first record of each process, by `proc_key`. `loads`: the load at launch of each process.
- `bins`: the binaries, each with the first 8 characters of its sha256.
- `files`, `tags`: the csv file names and the process tags, each once, in record order.
- `where`: the folder and the file names.

- Lines 176-177: for A-3 and the rows of runner bwx the cell also gives the number of processes and the first and the last tag.
- `stop`: the stop rule and the interval length in seconds (`min_ms` / 1000). For rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 `build_facts.py` sets both as constants (`whole pass` and 500 ms). It does not read them from the csv file [Ref3].
- `boot`: the boot label of an 8000 MT/s row, or the first 8 characters of the boot id. Speed, modules and boot are taken from the first record of the row.
- Lines 181-183: for F72d12 the Source cell also names `try6.txt`, `gaps.txt`, `boots.txt` and the `go.sh` log.
- Line 186: the load at launch, as one value or as the lowest to the highest value of the processes, with 2 decimal places.
- Line 187: the number of interval records and the number of processes of the row.
Appends the table with its 9 column titles. Then one bullet explains the column "Source". It inserts the number of the line of `r0.sh` that holds the sha256 of the binary of row R0.

Check against the DIMM report.
- `x10`: the oldread rates of the rows X1d10, X1d10b and BASEd10.
- The format in line 199 takes exactly two rates per row. These are oldread at position 0 of round 0 and of round 1.
- The build stops unless the report holds each pair as the text `a / b`, with 1 decimal place per rate (Python format `%.1f`).
- The report must also hold two fixed phrases on the runs with changed TXREQ settings.
- Then one bullet says which 10-module rows ran with changed settings. That assignment is template text. The check tests only that the texts are in the report. It does not test which pair the report gives for which settings.

Four bullets: the source of the boot numbers, the positions used from rows L-2 to L-4, R0 and R0b, the basis of the speed of the 2026-11-09 boot, and the firmware settings of the two boots. `fwx` supplies two values for the last bullet: the time at which the two TXREQ settings were set back, and the number of readable values of the settings list.

Checks for row F72d12. Its folder holds no boot id. The build stops unless all of these hold:
- `env.txt` of the folder holds none of the texts `boot`, `MemTotal` and `MT/s`. Its line count equals the count that the parser stored.
- The times lie in this order: the time of `try6.txt`, the launch line of the F72d12 process, its rc line, the first state line of the `go.sh` log (`go0`).
- That state line holds the boot id of `try6.txt`.
- The process lies inside the two times of row 0 of `boots.txt`, and inside the first and last log time of row 0 of `gaps.txt`.

Writes the proof as one bullet. The values are inserted from the files:
- The line count of `env.txt`, and the launch time and the rc time of the process.
- From `try6.txt`: its time, the boot id, MemTotal, the number of DIMM sockets, and the memory speed with the count that stands before it in the file. Each has its line number. The line number 1 of the time is typed in the template. The parser reads the time from the first line of the file [Ref2].
- The line of the `go.sh` log that holds the same boot id, with its time.
- Row 0 of `boots.txt` and row 0 of `gaps.txt`, with their times and line numbers.
The bullet ends with the limit: the speed and the module count were not read during the process.

`hw` holds one entry per process of rows L-1 to L-4, R0 and R0b, with the hardware error records in its window. `p13` holds the path of the saved journal (`p13['h5']`). `allrec` is the list of all these records. The build stops unless the list is not empty and every record has the severity `corrected`.
segments.heading: Section 4.1: hardware error records

segments.text: Writes the title of the block and four bullets: what one record is, what the window of a process is, the time resolution of 1 s, and which intervals the first table tests. These are the intervals that the sheet uses: oldread at position 0 and asmread at position 1. The bullets insert reference labels only, no number.

`kind_txt` returns the position of one error record `e` against the used intervals, as text.
- `outside`: the record touches no used interval.
- `inside` plus the interval: kernel, round, start and end in seconds after the process start, and the line of its I row. The start is the earliest thread start and the end is the latest thread end of the T rows [Ref2].
- `before or inside` plus the interval, for the kind `possible`. Line 270 stops the build unless the 2 s span of the record starts before the interval starts.

Builds the first table: one row per process of `hw`.
- `by_t` groups the records of the process by their journal time. That time has a resolution of 1 s.
- Line 278: the build stops unless all records of one second have the same position text.
- Columns: row, process tag, time of the launch line, time of the rc line, number of records in the window, journal time with the journal lines of the records, whole seconds after the launch line, position (`kind_txt`), and the source files.
- A process without records gets `-` in the three record columns.

- `ins`: the records of kind `inside`, each with its process. `pos`: the records of kind `possible`. Here the name `pos` is a list of records, not a position.
- `n_out`: the number of records of kind `outside`.
- Lines 291-292: the build stops unless `ins` holds exactly 2 records that lie in the same interval and have the same journal time.
- Lines 293-294: the same check for `pos`.

Finds the two used intervals with records, and the lowest asmread rate of the pool.
- `ivi`: the interval with the 2 records inside it. `ivp`: the interval of the 2 records of kind `possible`.
- `low_a`: the record with the lowest `GBps` in `P12a` (asmread at position 1 of rows L-1 to L-4). In the present sheet it is 288.54 GB/s, round 1 of process p2add in row L-2 [Ref4].
- Lines 298-300: the build stops unless `ivi` is asmread at position 1 of a row L-1 to L-4, and `low_a` is this interval (same row, same tag, same line of the I row).
- Lines 301-302: the build stops unless `ivp` is oldread at position 0, round 0, of row L-1.
- `P12a_wo`: the list `P12a` without the record `low_a`. `P12a` itself is not changed. Section 4.4 compares the 7200 MT/s rows with `P12a_wo` again.
- `c['hw']` stores these values for the later sections.

Five bullets with inserted values:
- The number of records in all windows.
- Row L-1: the 2 records that fall before or inside oldread, round 0, with the rate of that interval (`ivp['total']`).
- The process with the 2 records inside its asmread interval, with the rate of that interval (`ivi['total']`).
- The number of records outside the used intervals (`n_out`).
- The processes with 0 records in their window.
`total` is the sum over the T rows of the interval of bytes / elapsed_s / 1e9. A record holds the same value in `GBps` [Ref2] [Ref3]. It is printed with 2 decimal places.

Line 322: the build stops unless row 0 of `gaps.txt` shows `hwerr=0` and as many DIMMs as `try6.txt` shows DIMM sockets. Then three bullets:
- F72d12: the `hwerr` value of `gaps.txt`, and the note that the count rule of that file was not checked.
- Rerun: the template text "Insufficient data", with the reason that the Linux kernel log was not read.
- Template text on the rows whose records were not counted: the rows of runner bwx and the rows of other boots.

`hc` holds the comparison that `build_facts.py` made [Ref3].
- `crow`: every interval, of all kernels and positions, to which records can be assigned. That means: the records lie inside it, or it is the only interval that their 2 s span touches. Each entry has the field `diff`: the rate of the interval minus the rate of its other round, in GB/s.
- `cbor`: the records whose 2 s span touches two intervals. The sheet says that such records lie at the border of two intervals.
- `ccl`: the positions at which neither round has a record inside it or at its border. There `diff` is the rate of round 1 minus the rate of round 0. Only the processes with at least one record supply such positions.
- `sg`: prints a difference with 2 decimal places and its sign. A value that rounds to zero prints as `0.00`.
- Lines 340-342: the build stops when an other-round interval of the comparison has a record inside it or at its border.
segments.heading: Section 4.1: hypothesis on corrected records

segments.text:
- `rp`, `ri`: the entries of `crow` for the oldread interval `ivp` and for the asmread interval `ivi`. `more`: the entries of the intervals that the sheet does not use.
- Lines 346-348: the build stops unless each of the two used intervals has exactly one entry and all other entries are in `more`. The records of `rp` must lie `before or inside`. The records of every other entry must lie `inside`.
- `n_more`, `n_bor`: the number of records in the entries of `more`, and the number of records at the borders.
- Lines 351-352: the build stops unless these two numbers add up to `n_out`, `crow` has more than 2 entries, at least one border exists, and every border lies between exactly 2 intervals.

The threshold and the groups of this comparison.
- `LIM` = 1.0 GB/s. A difference between the two rounds counts only above this value. This file sets the value. The view is not part of the fixed rules (line 377).
- `low`: the entries of `crow` that lie more than 1.0 GB/s below their other round, the largest drop first.
- `rest`: all other entries of `crow`.
- `cbig`: the positions without records at which the two rounds differ by more than 1.0 GB/s.
- `cmax`: the position without records with the largest difference between the two rounds.
- `low_in`: the entries of `low` whose difference is smaller than the difference of `cmax`. Both are compared without their sign.

Four checks. The build stops unless the data show each pattern that the text below states.
- Lines 359-362: `low` is not empty, and its largest drop is the asmread interval `ri`. Every entry of `rest` differs by less than 1.0 GB/s. The oldread interval `rp` is in `rest` and is higher than its other round. At least one entry of `rest` is lower than its other round.
- Lines 363-364: exactly one entry of `low` differs by at least as much as `cmax`, and `ri` differs by more than `cmax`. `low_in` and `cbig` are not empty.
- Lines 365-368: `cmax` lies in the process of `ivi`, at the position directly after it. Round 1 is the lower round at `cmax`, and `ivi` is in round 1.
- Lines 369-370: the positions without records come from the same processes as the entries of `crow`.

`bdiff`: the differences of the border intervals against their other round. `c['hw']['cmp']` stores the counts, the groups, `cmax` and `LIM` for section 6. The stored function `lst` joins texts with commas, and with `and` before the last text.

Writes the hypothesis as one bullet, an intro text and the second table. The table has one row per entry of `crow`. Its columns:
- Row, process, and the interval (kernel, round, position) with the line of its I row.
- The journal lines of the records, and their position (`inside` or `before or inside`).
- The rate of the interval, and the rate of the other round with the line of its I row.
- The difference (`sg`), whether the sheet uses the interval, and the sources.
The rates are printed with 2 decimal places. The difference is computed before rounding.

Names the test loops of this block that the word list of the sheet does not define.
- `loops`: the kernel names of `crow`, of the border intervals and of `cmax`, without the six names of `in_words`. They are sorted by the name without its trailing number, then by that number.
- Lines 396-397 read section F2 of `FINDINGS.md`, from the heading `## F2.` to the next line that starts with `## `.
- The build stops unless every name appears in that section as a whole word, and all rows of the comparison are rows of bwx12 or bwx11.
- One sentence then lists the names.

`btxt` holds one text per border: the number of records, the row and the process, the seconds after the launch line, the journal lines, the two kernels and the round. The build stops unless the two intervals of each border are in the same round and at neighbour positions. `lst` joins texts with commas, and with `and` before the last text.

Writes six bullets. The first four insert values:
- Records outside the used intervals: `n_more` fall inside the intervals of `more`, and `n_bor` lie at a border. The border intervals differ from their other round by the lowest to the highest value of `bdiff`.
- What fits: `len(low)` of the `len(crow)` intervals lie more than `LIM` below their other round. The drops are printed as positive values, the smallest first.
- What does not fit: the `len(rest)` other intervals, with the lowest and the highest of their differences, and the two rates of oldread of row L-1.
- Limit: the number of positions without records (`len(ccl)`), how many of them differ by more than `LIM` (`len(cbig)`), the largest such difference, and the number of entries of `low_in`. The count in "and 1 ... is above them" is typed in the template. Line 363 tests it.
- Template text: the comparison is not a test of the hypothesis.
- Template text: the measurement that would confirm or reject the hypothesis.

- `a1o`, `a2o`, `a3o`: the records of rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 with `binary` = `bw_old` and `kernel` = `read`.
- Lines 447-449: the range table. Its rows are part A of the rerun (`A72o`, sessions 1 to 3), A-1, A-2, A-3 and the pool A-1 to A-3 (`A80o`). In the present sheet `A72o` holds 18 intervals and `A80o` holds 21 intervals [Ref4].
- Lines 450-451: `cmps` tests the range of `A72o` against four scopes: A-1, A-2, A-3 and the pool. Only the pool has `decides` = True. So only the test against the pool gets a wording.
- Each test is also stored in `V['q2_rows']` with part `A` and kernel `bw_old read`.
segments.heading: Section 4.2: old read kernel, part A (`bw_old read`)

segments.text:
A check per process of part A.
- `b80` is now the range of the pool A-1 to A-3. In line 150 the same name held the boot labels.
- `N['pa']` has one entry per session and round. `p['old']` holds the 3 `bw_old read` intervals of that process.
- A sentence is noted in `outs` when the lowest of the 3 rates lies above the highest rate of the pool.
- A sentence is also noted when the highest of the 3 rates lies below the lowest rate of the pool.

Three bullets:
- The wording of the test against the pool (`cAo['wording']`), with n at 7200 MT/s and n at 8000 MT/s.
- The width of the 8000 MT/s range in percent with 1 decimal place (`cAo['width']`), as the size that the test cannot exclude.
- Only when `outs` is not empty: the sentence "The 7200 MT/s range is wider than the 8000 MT/s range", the noted sentences, and the number of the other processes. Lines 464 to 466 do not compare the two widths. `facts_text.py` compares them after the call of `section4`, when it builds section 0 [Ref1].

- `lrows(k, pos)`: one table row per row L-1 to L-4, with its records of kernel `k` at position `pos`. `orows` does the same for rows R0 and R0b.
- `x2o`, `x2a`: the oldread records and the asmread records of row X2d12.
- `sL`: the description of part L. It takes the start-state text of process T72L1 from `evd` and writes it for all three processes.
- No `need` call of this file tests that T72L2 and T72L3 have the same start state. In `facts.json` the records of all three processes hold a `gap_s` of 5 s.
- `sI`: the description of control I.
segments.heading: Section 4.2: old read kernel, part L (`oldread`)

segments.text: The range table of oldread at position 0. Rows, in order: part L (`L72o`), L-1, L-2, L-3, L-4, the pool L-1 to L-4 (`P12o`), R0, R0b, the pool with R0 and R0b (`PALLo`), X2d12, F72d12 (`F72o`) and control I (`I72o`). Each row gives n, the lowest to the highest rate, and the median. Row X2d12 is shown only: no range test of this file uses it.

The range tests of oldread.
- `l1o`, `l1a`: the oldread records and the asmread records of row L-1.
- `sc_o`: three 8000 MT/s scopes for oldread: L-1 alone, the pool L-1 to L-4, and the pool with R0 and R0b. Only the pool L-1 to L-4 has `decides` = True.
- `sc_a`: the same three scopes for asmread. Section 4.4 uses it.
- `cmps` tests three 7200 MT/s rows against the three scopes: part L, F72d12 and control I. That gives 9 tests. Each test is stored in `V['q2_rows']` with part `L` and kernel `oldread`.
- F72d12 and control I are tested as their own rows. Their records are not added to the list of part L.

- `kLo1` is the test of part L against L-1 alone.
- Line 486 stops the build when the range of part L overlaps L-1 alone or the pool with R0 and R0b. It tests the overlap only, not the direction.
- The bullet prints the wording of the test against the pool L-1 to L-4 (`cLo['wording']`) and both n.
- The words "Part L is lower" are template text. `facts_text.py` tests this direction against the pool L-1 to L-4 before it calls `section4` [Ref1].

The size of the difference between part L and the pool L-1 to L-4, from `cLo`. `a` is the range of part L and `b` is the range of the pool.
- `near` = -`dist` = b.lo - a.hi: the distance of the nearest ends. Present value: 1.24 GB/s, 0.3 % of b.lo [Ref4].
- `far` = b.hi - a.lo: the distance of the farthest ends. Present value: 8.45 GB/s, 1.8 % of b.lo.
- `mid` = b.med - a.med: the distance of the medians. Present value: 6.27 GB/s, 1.3 % of b.med.
- Percent values: `near` and `far` are divided by b.lo, `mid` by b.med, each times 100. Line 490 stores `near`, `mid` and their two percent values in `c['oldL']` for sections 4.9 and 6.
- Line 491: the build stops unless `near` is below 1 % and `mid` is above 1 %. So it passes only when the median of the pool lies above the median of part L.
- The bullet prints GB/s values with 2 decimal places and percent values with 1 decimal place. All are computed before rounding. It also prints the width of the pool range (`cLo['width']`).

Two bullets:
- Template text on rule V1 point 4: the rule does not say which distance counts. Its last sentence says that the distance of the nearest ends is below 1 % and that the distance of the medians is above 1 %. Line 491 tests this.
- F72d12 and control I: their two ranges (`cFo['a']`, `cIo['a']`) and the range of the pool (`cFo['b']`).
Three statements of the second bullet are template text here:
- Both rows are runs of the same line in the same 7200 MT/s boot. For control I the integrity checks `args` and `boot` of `build_facts.py` test it. For F72d12 the integrity check `args-R8` and lines 219 to 222 test it [Ref3].
- Both ranges overlap the pool. `facts_text.py` tests it before it calls `section4` [Ref1].
- Both rows were launched at a 1-minute load average below 1.0. For control I, `facts_text.py` tests it before it calls `section4` [Ref1]. For F72d12, no `need` call of this file tests it. The present load at launch of F72d12 is 0.34 [Ref4].

Checks on the error records in oldread intervals. `ep` is one of the 2 records that fall before or inside oldread, round 0 of row L-1.
- Lines 504-505: the build stops when a record of kind `inside` or `possible` belongs to another used oldread interval.
- Lines 507-509: the same check for the oldread intervals at every position (field `every`). Row R0 holds oldread at two positions.
- The bullet prints the round, the row and the rate of the one oldread interval with records. Its count "2 corrected records" is typed in the template. Lines 245 and 293 test it.

Line 513: the build stops unless oldread of part C overlaps the pool L-1 to L-4 (`cCo`). The last bullet of this block is template text with one inserted value, the start-state text of T72L1. Its statements and their tests:
- Among the bwx12 runs at 7200 MT/s, only the range of part L lies below the pool. Line 513 tests the overlap of part C. `facts_text.py` tests part L, F72d12 and control I before it calls `section4` [Ref1].
- In the view by start state, part C also lies below the bwx12 processes of the pool that started after 120-thread work. Line 577 tests it.
- Against the other-binary processes with that kind of start state, part C overlaps. Line 606 tests it.
- Each memory speed has one boot. Line 152 tests it for the 8000 MT/s rows of its list. For the 7200 MT/s records that check is true whatever the run files contain. The explanation of lines 150 to 152 names the tests of the 7200 MT/s boot.
